content_preview.title: AWS Launches API Portal and AWS WAF AI Security, Routing MCP and A2A Traffic Through Bedrock Guardrails
content_preview.summary: AWS launched API Portal to find shadow MCP and A2A endpoints, plus an AWS WAF AI Security rule group that screens their traffic through Amazon Bedrock Guardrails.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Amazon Web Services has launched a new feature in Amazon API Gateway called API Portal, which finds API and AI endpoints across an AWS account or organization, alongside two new AWS WAF managed rule groups, API Security and AI Security, which screen traffic to those endpoints — including large language model (LLM) endpoints, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and Agent2Agent (A2A) servers — for abuse. According to [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/11/waf-ai-en...

editor_notes.content_quality: Dense, well-organized bullet-point structure covering six distinct aspects of the launch (discovery, rule groups, protocol checks, Guardrails inspection, availability/pricing, customer reaction). Technical detail is accurate and appropriately hedged where AWS's own disclosures left gaps (no pricing figures, no exfiltration-detection ship date, no customer-adoption numbers).
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources read in full from decompressed .html.gz snapshots (sha256-verified against manifest). Performed a literal, exhaustive quote-by-quote audit of every double-quoted span in the body (~20 quotes) against the raw extracted text of both pages: the API-discovery/protection description, the shadow/zombie/orphaned API definitions, the two rule groups' coverage descriptions, the OWASP BOLA reference, the MCP/A2A protocol-version list, the Baseline-tier header/body-mismatch example, the Bedrock Guardrails InvokeGuardrailsCheck description and default-block behavior, the 7-region availability list, the pricing disclaimer, the pending data-exfiltration-detection gap, the three-callers framing, the tools/list/agent-card self-description mechanism, and the full Mike Hasani customer quote with name/title/company — every single one matched the raw source text verbatim (whitespace/typographic-apostrophe differences aside). No fabricated or misattributed quotes found anywhere in the piece.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated specifics. The article explicitly and accurately notes what neither AWS publication discloses (pricing figures, adoption numbers, competitor comparisons) rather than inventing placeholders.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; correctly attributes the Mike Hasani quote as AWS's own selected customer testimonial, not independent verification.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald coverage of API Portal or AWS WAF AI Security found.
editor_notes.prompt_injection_review: The automated scanner's error-severity finding on the AWS Security Blog URL was manually investigated by reading the flagged excerpt in its raw HTML context: it is one row of an ordinary documentation table titled 'Bedrock Guardrails check / What it looks for', listing 'Prompt attack: Jailbreaks, prompt injection, and attempts to extract the system prompt' as the threat category the new feature screens for — a plain description of the product's own capability, not an instruction addressed to an AI agent reading the page. Confirmed false positive; overridden per policy after reading the raw snapshot in context.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A rigorously sourced, entirely accurate News article on AWS's new API/AI endpoint discovery and protection launch, with every one of roughly 20 quotes independently verified verbatim and one automated false-positive investigated and overridden. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurately verified cloud-infrastructure coverage for a defined DevOps/security audience; a notable but incremental AWS feature launch, not broad-audience or industry-changing.
